pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## What is this?

Steamworks Additions is a small sister plugin of Steamworks: **atmosphere props** for the towns, breweries and stations. No rotation, no stress - just brass, copper and a bell that knows what time it is. It runs next to Steamworks but never needs a shaft.

### The props

* **Steam Clock** - a brass tower clock with a floating time plate; it strikes its bell on every in-game hour.
* **Brass Railing** - iron posts with brass bars that join each other automatically. Queue dividers, quay edges, garden borders.
* **Vent Grille** - a copper vent with green slats. On a wall or free-standing, it tells everyone that something steams behind this facade.

### In the game

* Every prop has a workbench recipe (see the [recipes page](/recipes) or `/zukan`), shows up in your recipe book, and is picked back up by left-clicking it (twice by default).
* Staff hand them out with `/sa give <player> <prop>`; `/sa list` shows what exists.
* The props save themselves in the chunk, exactly like Steamworks machines: reload a chunk, the prop is back on its spot.

### Good to know

* The clock reads the *world* clock (a Minecraft day is 20 minutes), so it strikes every 50 real-time minutes. It only makes noise and ticks while players are nearby - an empty quarter is silent and costs nothing.
* Nothing here touches the Steamworks network. You can run Additions without a single shaft in sight (though a clock on top of a pumping station does look fantastic).

[The Steam Clock](/wiki?page=additions-clock) · [Brass Railing & Vent](/wiki?page=additions-brass)

pages.title: The Steam Clock
pages.content:
## The Steam Clock

A two-block brass tower: iron column, brass case with an ivory dial, two small golden bells under a dark roof and a finial on top. It tells the town what time it is - twice.


* [What it does](/wiki?page=additions-clock-what-it-does)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=additions-clock-good-to-know)
* [Crafting](/wiki?page=additions-clock-crafting)
* [Placing and moving](/wiki?page=additions-clock-placing-and-moving)

pages.title: What it does
pages.content:
* A **floating time plate** above the dial always reads the current in-game hour, e.g. `07:00`.
* On **every in-game hour** the bell strikes: a clear brass bell tone, pitched per hour, and at **noon and midnight it rings twice**.
* A small steam puff comes out of the top when it strikes, so you can see from across the square who is late.

Back to [The Steam Clock](/wiki?page=additions-clock)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* A full Minecraft day is 20 minutes, so an hour passes every 50 real-time minutes. The clock is tied to the world clock - sleep through the night and the clock jumps with it.
* The clock only ticks and strikes **while players are within about 24 blocks**. A clock in an abandoned quarter is perfectly silent and costs the server nothing.
* It stands free (the base block is solid, you bump into it) and needs no power at all.

Back to [The Steam Clock](/wiki?page=additions-clock)

pages.title: Crafting
pages.content:
Shapeless: **1 Clock + 2 Copper Ingots + 2 Gold Nuggets + 1 Redstone** → 1 Steam Clock.

Back to [The Steam Clock](/wiki?page=additions-clock)

pages.title: Placing and moving
pages.content:
Right-click with the clock item to place it (needs 2 blocks of air above its spot). Left-click twice to take it back; the time plate disappears with it.

Staff: `/sa give <player> steam_clock`.

Back to [The Steam Clock](/wiki?page=additions-clock)

pages.title: Brass Railing
pages.content:
Iron posts with two brass bars. The railing **joins its neighbours automatically**: place a second one next to it and the bars grow into one run; corners, T-junctions and end posts pick the right piece by themselves - exactly like the garden fence, only with more brass.

* Walk over it: it is low (you bump into the posts, but you can step along).
* Craft: **3 Iron Ingots + 2 Sticks** → **4 railing pieces**.
* Classic uses: queue lines at the station and ticket kiosk, quay edges, the brewery terrace, keeping the horses out of the flower beds.

Back to [Brass Railing & Vent Grille](/wiki?page=additions-brass)

pages.title: Vent Grille
pages.content:
A copper frame with three green-brass slats over a dark opening, with bolts in the corners.

* **Mounts on any wall** - right-click a wall face with the item and it hangs flat, facing outward. On the ground it leans against the block you placed it on.
* Craft: **2 Copper Ingots + 2 Iron Nuggets** → 1 grille.
* It is decoration that tells a story: put one above a kettle line, on a boiler wall or along the brewery's back street, and everyone knows where the steam comes from. (It does not connect to real pipes - that would be too easy.)

Back to [Brass Railing & Vent Grille](/wiki?page=additions-brass)

pages.title: Taking them back
pages.content:
Left-click twice like every prop. Railing sections come apart per piece: take one from the middle and the neighbours re-shape themselves the next time they load.

Staff: `/sa give <player> brass_railing|vent_grille`.

Back to [Brass Railing & Vent Grille](/wiki?page=additions-brass)
